blocks.text:
After breakfast, transfer to the airport and fly to Foz do Iguaçu.

After Rio, the scenery and the experience change dramatically. Here, water takes centre stage. The Iguaçu River divides into hundreds of streams that plunge from heights of up to 80 m. You can hear the roar before reaching the main viewpoints, and spray hangs constantly in the air. It settles on your skin, clothes and the rocks, so you feel the presence of the falls long before the main panorama comes into view.

blocks.text:
A tour of the Brazilian side of the falls in the national park.

The trail leads through the forest, gradually approaching the cascades. It then opens onto a panorama of the almost 3-kilometre system of waterfalls at the meeting point of Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay. The name “Iguaçu” means “Big Water” in Guarani, and the falls are associated with a volcanic eruption and shifts in the Earth's crust.

Above the cascades, the river flows more calmly. Then the water plunges down in countless streams. The paths lead to the most spectacular sections.

The main stop is Devil's Throat, a semicircular gorge where powerful streams converge. The water falls in an unbroken wall, throwing up clouds of spray. The walkways come very close to the torrent, bringing the water almost to eye level. In sunny weather, rainbows appear above the gorge.
